answer: A concrete mechanism is bonded stake with slashing tied to peer attestation. Every agent locks collateral before acting, and validators only attest an identity whose deposit is real and at risk. A sybil attacker cannot mint hollow identities cheaply: each new account demands the same stake, so flooding the network with fakes costs a flood of real capital. When peers detect duplicates and slash them, the attacker loses that capital. Fraud becomes like buying copper and timber in bulk for a structure no one trusts, paying full value for each duplicate while an honest agent pays once.
